title: An extraction after the first sequence can run past its sequence end
body: `extraction` in `libsufr/src/search.rs` clips the context after a hit at the end of its sequence. It compares `seq_end`, a position in the whole text, with positions relative to the sequence start. For a hit in any sequence after the first, the comparison is between two different coordinate systems, so the context can run past the end of the hit's sequence into the next one. The site carries a TODO. Found during sufr-28ca67; the CLI tests pin the current output, so the fix changes a golden file.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4be42394
notes.text: At cff9fb6 the site is `extraction` (`search.rs:341-372`), with the TODO at :353-355. `seq_end` is an absolute position. `context_end` (`search.rs:362-365`) compares it with `relative_suffix_start + len`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Jack decided on 2026-11-03 to fix this before sufr-5cf0b7, the search tests, so the hand-derived window expectations are right. The fix also stops a window at the last byte of its sequence: today the window on the first sequence includes the delimiter, ABC:4-9 prints ACGT% on fixture 2, and after the fix it prints ACGT at 4-8. The two inline CLI expectations at cli.rs:561 and 596 and any .out file with a window at a sequence end move with the fix.
